summary: The note explores how original playwriting in community theater celebrates local stories, centered on The Oak Leaf Theater and the September 2023 premiere of Alice Monroe's "Whispers from the Old Mill". It covers the collaborative writing process, audience participation, intergenerational and youth engagement, opportunities for new talent, economic benefits for local businesses, diversity and inclusion, and the healing role of storytelling, with quotes from various local figures.
one_line: Original local playwriting at The Oak Leaf Theater strengthens community through shared stories, new talent, economic boosts, inclusion, and healing.
key_facts: Alice Monroe's play "Whispers from the Old Mill" premiered on September 15 (2023) at The Oak Leaf Theater, a quaint theater in the center of town.
Greg Taylor is the artistic director at The Oak Leaf Theater and says there is "an invigorating sense of belonging when the narratives stem from your own backyard."
The theater committee hosts local playwright workshops every year in early October; the workshop began on October 3, 2023.
Eleanor Rigby, a seasoned playwright, has mentored many amateur writers since the workshop's inception and says the goal is "the most truthful portrait of our collective life."
Jordan Willis's breakthrough piece "Saturday Market Blues" is set to stage in November 2023.
Michael Rodriguez went from a minor background role to the lead in "Echoes through the Alleyway," scheduled to premiere in December 2023.
Marianne Phillips, a longstanding patron, says attending local performances feels "more like a conversation than a presentation."
Sophia Duran, a high school drama teacher involved in youth theater development, says local-tale theater instills in young people a sense of history and connection to their roots.
Open auditions and equal opportunity policies are making community theaters a democratizing space for budding actors, directors, and writers.
Lisa Chen, a restaurant owner and chef near The Oak Leaf Theater, says show nights are some of her busiest, as people discuss plays over dinner.
Jean-Claude Parker, an Afro-Caribbean playwright whose works highlight immigrant experiences, says theater has the power to build bridges.
Dr. Andrea Gonzalez, a therapist and playwriting enthusiast, says narratives let communities confront realities and heal from collective wounds.
